threats.title: Customer documents sent to third-party LLM
threats.description: Full document text, including personal data, leaves the tenant for the hosted LLM API; the design states no data processing terms, region or retention settings.
threats.control: Use an enterprise endpoint with zero data retention and region pinning under a DPA; redact personal data before the prompt; complete a DPIA.

refs.quote: The prompt and full document text are sent to the hosted LLM API

threats.title: Indirect prompt injection via uploaded documents
threats.description: An attacker who uploads a crafted document can inject instructions that the summariser follows, and the summariser can write to the Case DB.
threats.control: Treat document text as untrusted data and constrain what the agent can do (see child threats T14, T15).

refs.quote: Calls the LLM and executes the tool calls it requests

threats.title: Cluster-admin credential used for deployment
threats.description: Anyone who compromises a pipeline job can reuse the cluster-admin kubeconfig to take full control of the production cluster.
threats.control: Workload identity federation (OIDC) with a namespace-scoped deploy role; no static credentials in CI.

refs.quote: uses a cluster-admin kubeconfig stored as a repository secret

threats.title: Any file type accepted without content checks
threats.description: An attacker can upload weaponised or malformed files that are passed to parsers downstream.
threats.control: Allow-list file types, enforce size limits, AV/CDR scan before any parsing, fail closed on errors.

refs.quote: The Intake Service accepts any file type up to 100 MB

threats.title: Long-lived customer session tokens
threats.description: A stolen session token remains usable for up to 24 hours with no stated revocation.
threats.control: Short-lived access tokens with refresh rotation, revocation on logout and password change, MFA for account changes.

refs.quote: receive a session token valid for 24 hours

threats.title: Guessable document paths
threats.description: Blob paths use sequential case numbers, so any path that accepts a case number could expose another customer's documents.
threats.control: Random object keys, per-request ownership checks, SAS tokens scoped to one object with short expiry.

refs.quote: Blob paths use the sequential case number

threats.title: Untrusted pull requests can influence the pipeline
threats.description: PR builds share runners and secrets with main-branch builds, and third-party actions are unpinned.
threats.control: Separate the untrusted PR path from the trusted build and deploy path (see child threats T21, T24).

refs.quote: PR builds run on the shared self-hosted runners used for main-branch builds

threats.title: Single shared vector index for all customers
threats.description: Retrieval for one case can surface another customer's content because the index is not partitioned.
threats.control: Per-tenant namespaces with filters enforced server-side, not in the prompt.

refs.quote: embedded into a single shared vector index

threats.title: Review Portal database connection not specified
threats.description: The design does not say how the Review Portal authenticates to the Case DB or whether TLS is enforced.
threats.control: Managed identity, TLS 1.2+, least-privilege stored procedures.

threats.title: No audit trail for case changes
threats.description: There is no record of who changed a case or approved an AI summary, including changes made by the agent.
threats.control: Append-only audit log capturing user and agent identity for every case change.

threats.title: No limit on document length sent to the model
threats.description: Large or adversarial uploads drive token cost and throttling of the LLM service.
threats.control: Per-tenant quotas, maximum tokens per job, circuit breaker on spend.

refs.quote: There is no limit on document length

threats.title: Reviewers approve summaries without seeing sources
threats.description: Reviewers see only the AI summary, so incorrect or manipulated summaries can be approved into the case record.
threats.control: Show source citations next to the summary; require reviewer attestation; sample QA.

refs.quote: sign in to the Review Portal with Entra ID SSO and approve the summary

threats.title: Customers not told documents are AI-processed
threats.description: The upload journey has no notice of AI processing or transfer to a third party.
threats.control: Privacy notice and consent text at upload; record the notice version accepted.

threats.title: Untrusted document text mixed into the system prompt
threats.description: The Prompt Builder concatenates the system prompt, document text and retrieved chunks with no separation, so injected text is read as instructions.
threats.control: Spotlighting: wrap untrusted text in delimiters with an explicit data-only instruction; keep system prompt separate; strip instruction-like content.

refs.quote: concatenates the system prompt, document text and top-5 retrieved chunks into one prompt

threats.title: Agent executes write tools with service credentials
threats.description: Any instruction the model follows can call update_case using the service's database credentials, with no user context or approval.
threats.control: Least agency: read-only tools by default; writes become proposals approved in the Review Portal; user-scoped tokens for tool calls (see T26-T28).

refs.quote: Tool calls are executed with the service's database credentials

threats.title: Parsers share a container with the orchestrator
threats.description: A parser or OCR exploit in a crafted file gains the orchestrator's credentials and network access.
threats.control: Run extraction in a separate sandboxed container with no credentials and no egress; patch parsing libraries from a curated repository.

refs.quote: runs in the same container as the Agent Orchestrator

threats.title: Retrieval query has no tenant filter
threats.description: Top-5 retrieval runs across the shared index, so chunks from other customers' documents enter the prompt.
threats.control: Server-side tenant filter on every query; per-tenant namespaces.

refs.quote: top-5 retrieved chunks
single shared vector index

threats.title: LLM API key held in an environment variable
threats.description: The API key can be read by anything running in the pod, including a compromised parser, and reused to impersonate the service.
threats.control: Managed identity or Key Vault reference with rotation; separate key per environment; egress restricted to the LLM endpoint.

refs.quote: using an API key stored in an environment variable

threats.title: Validator checks format only
threats.description: The Response Validator checks the JSON schema but not whether the content is grounded or safe to write.
threats.control: Add grounding checks against source text and block outputs containing instructions or links before writing.

refs.quote: Checks the summary against the JSON schema

threats.title: Conversation cache holds document content for 7 days
threats.description: Redis keeps prompts and outputs containing personal data for 7 days with no stated encryption or access control.
threats.control: Minimise cached content, 24-hour TTL, Redis AUTH with TLS, private endpoint.

refs.quote: Conversation state is cached in Redis for 7 days

threats.title: Repository secrets exposed to pull request jobs
threats.description: Code from a pull request runs on shared runners with access to repository secrets, including the deploy credential.
threats.control: No secrets for PR workflows; ephemeral isolated runners for untrusted code; environment protection rules for secrets.

refs.quote: with access to repository secrets

threats.title: Cluster-admin kubeconfig stored as a repository secret
threats.description: A static cluster-admin credential in repository secrets gives full cluster control to anyone who can read secrets.
threats.control: OIDC federation to a namespace-scoped deploy identity; remove the kubeconfig secret.

refs.quote: uses a cluster-admin kubeconfig stored as a repository secret

threats.title: Images deployed without signature verification
threats.description: A tampered or substituted image in the registry is deployed to production without detection.
threats.control: Sign images at build (Sigstore or Notation) with SLSA provenance; admission policy in AKS rejects unsigned images.

refs.quote: Image signatures are not verified at deployment

threats.title: Third-party actions referenced by mutable tags
threats.description: A compromised or re-tagged marketplace action runs with pipeline privileges.
threats.control: Pin actions by full commit SHA; allow-list approved actions; automated update PRs.

refs.quote: Workflows reference marketplace actions by tag

threats.title: Static service principal secret for the registry
threats.description: A long-lived secret for pushing images can be stolen from the runner and used to push malicious images.
threats.control: OIDC federation for ACR push; scoped push-only role.

refs.quote: pushes them to Azure Container Registry using a service principal secret

threats.title: update_case can change any case without approval
threats.description: The model can set any case's status and summary, with no check that the case belongs to the current job and no human approval.
threats.control: Replace with propose_case_update limited to the current case ID; the reviewer approves in the Review Portal.

refs.quote: update_case (writes case status and summary)

threats.title: Tool router executes model requests without validation
threats.description: Tool names and parameters from model output are executed as given, with no allow-list or parameter validation.
threats.control: Allow-list tools per job type; schema-validate and bound every parameter; log every tool call with the job ID.

refs.quote: executes the tool calls it requests

threats.title: search_cases is not scoped to the customer
threats.description: Injected instructions can make the model search and summarise other customers' cases.
threats.control: Scope search_cases to the current customer using a user-scoped token or row-level security.

refs.quote: search_cases (reads the Case DB)

threats.frameworks: ASI06; LLM02:2026; LINDDUN DD; LINDDUN L
threats.title: Tool results persisted in conversation memory
threats.description: Results from search_cases, possibly other customers' data, are stored in the cache and reused in later prompts.
threats.control: Do not persist tool results; partition memory per case; 24-hour TTL.

refs.quote: Conversation state is cached in Redis for 7 days

recommendations.title: Least-agency design for the summariser agent
recommendations.description: Read-only tools by default; replace update_case with propose_case_update limited to the current case and approved by a reviewer; user-scoped tokens and row-level security for tool calls; tool allow-list and parameter validation in the router.

recommendations.title: Isolate untrusted content processing
recommendations.description: AV/CDR scan and type allow-list at intake; run text extraction in a separate sandboxed container with no credentials or egress; spotlight untrusted text in prompts.

recommendations.title: Keyless, least-privilege pipeline
recommendations.description: OIDC workload identity federation for ACR and AKS with namespace-scoped roles; remove repository secrets; isolated ephemeral runners with no secrets for PRs; pin actions by SHA.

recommendations.title: Signed and verified artifacts
recommendations.description: Sign images and attach SLSA provenance at build; enforce signature verification with an AKS admission policy.

recommendations.title: Tenant isolation for documents, retrieval and agent memory
recommendations.description: Random blob keys with ownership checks; per-tenant vector namespaces with server-side filters; per-case agent memory with short TTL and no stored tool results.

recommendations.title: Governed use of the third-party LLM
recommendations.description: Enterprise endpoint with zero retention and region pinning under a DPA and DPIA; personal data redaction; key held in Key Vault or replaced by managed identity; token quotas; customer notice at upload.

recommendations.title: Session hardening at the edge
recommendations.description: Short-lived access tokens with refresh rotation and revocation.

recommendations.title: Accountable human review
recommendations.description: Append-only audit log of case changes with user and agent identity; show sources beside summaries; grounding checks before write.

questions.question: How does the Review Portal authenticate to the Case DB, and is TLS enforced?
Where are case changes and summary approvals audited, and who can alter the audit records?
What notice do customers receive that documents are processed by AI and a third-party provider?
What data processing terms, region and retention settings apply to the hosted LLM API?
Is the Redis cache encrypted, network-isolated and protected with authentication?
Are the self-hosted runners ephemeral, and which workflows can read which secrets?
